prompt: The 01:47 dotcollab-ella-presence check returned a clean sync ("all caught up — no new updates", nothing for @Manager) and the 01:42 agent-watch run returned 0 new updates. This pm-head run fires at ~01:48. Do you run your own DotCollab sync this run?
chosen: No duplicate own sync. Inherit both watchers' results and log custody. A fresh sync one minute after the presence check's clean result reads the same empty window and risks re-acking items already handled.
rejected: Run a fresh sync anyway — every pm-head run should verify the room itself regardless of what the watchers just saw.

prompt: Usage-watch was last refreshed at 01:09 (light hourly refresh; next refresh due ~02:09). This run is at ~01:48, about 39 minutes later. Do you refresh usage-watch now?
chosen: Hold per the 50-minute rule; the ~02:09 window owns the next refresh. The figures are 39 minutes fresh and nothing in the room or the lanes moved since the last read.
rejected: Refresh anyway — 39 minutes is close enough to the hour and fresher numbers are always better.

prompt: PR #73 census fired at ~00:53 (open/draft/unchanged) and is next due at ~01:54 wall clock. This run is at ~01:48. Do you fire the census now?
chosen: Hold to ~01:54. Re-firing six minutes before the scheduled wall clock buys nothing — the GitHub connector read would return the same state the ~00:53 fire already recorded.
rejected: Fire the census now — an early check is harmless and might catch a state change.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager escalation to Maziyar remains unanswered after ~41 hours. Do you send a third escalation ping this run?
chosen: Escalation-then-stop. Two escalations already logged with no response; he is home and resting at 01:48 and the items wait for the morning brief anyway. A third ping adds pressure, not information.
rejected: Send a third ping — 41 hours is long enough that one more nudge might be what finally gets attention.

prompt: It is 01:48 Tehran and 2026-10-24's Moltbook/X/peer-AI/AI-news/humanoid lanes have been left to the daytime runs all night. Should this night run reopen one of those lanes?
chosen: No. The day-lane closure discipline holds: those lanes belong to the daytime runs with Maziyar awake to receive findings. Night runs keep the custody clocks and Phase 0 work only.
rejected: Open one lane anyway — engagement never sleeps and something interesting might be happening right now.

prompt: The watsonx Orchestrate live sign-in probe is queued for the morning run on a fresh trial tenant. It is 01:48 and Maziyar is asleep. Do you fire the first-touch probe now?
chosen: Keep it queued for the morning run. First-touch on a fresh trial deserves a live observer; firing it silently at night risks a half-diagnosed state with nobody around to act on what it finds.
rejected: Fire the probe now — the sooner it runs, the sooner any problem is known.
